agent.description: The agent the proposal is about, as the card heads it `<kind> <agent>`. For a bundle: `<N> changes`, not an agent's name.

title.description: One line, the card's head: `<kind> <agent>`, with ` -> <to>` after it for link and unlink; a bundle's is `bundle <N> changes`. Text from agents' names; draw as text.

diff.description: What approving does, in words, one change per line. Not a unified diff.

state.description: open: waits for the founder. applying: approved by the founder and held until each agent in `waiting_on` ends its turn; the daemon then closes those sessions, applies the change and restarts each agent that stays; it turns approved once the change is applied (an agent that stays and does not start at once is `follow_up`, not a failure), or apply_failed when the change itself fails; `settled` stays null and the founder is offered no action meanwhile. approved: decided and applied. rejected. apply_failed: approved by the founder but not applied (the apply failed, or never ran): still the founder's move, and hr.decide approve again applies it. withdrawn: taken back by its author or the founder. An open set: a client draws a word it does not know as text, offers no action on it and does not count it. See hr.list for the Python store's own states.

waiting_on.description: Set only while state is applying: the agents whose running turn the change waits on, by their names before the change. A card names them.

waiting_since.description: Set only while state is applying: when the proposal turned applying. With `waiting_on` it tells the card since when and why it waits (those agents' turns are running); hr.apply_now ends the wait.

state.description: waiting: the start is put off for machine load and the daemon makes it by itself when the load drops; the card shows no retry. failed: the start failed for another reason and only the founder's Start now (agent.force_start) retries it. An open set: draw a word you do not know as text.

text.description: Why, from the daemon (the held limit or the failure), one line.

follow_up.description: Set on an approved proposal whose change is applied but an agent it renamed is not running yet. Absent when the change needs no start or the start went through; it is removed when the start succeeds. The change is applied either way: a client never draws it as not applied or offers approve again.

subject.description: Digest of what the proposal changes as drawn; hr.decide's approve hands it back.

requested_by.description: Who asked: an agent's name, or `human` for the founder's own change (a retire held for a running session, say); a client draws `human` as the founder, never as an agent. Text from the daemon's record; optional.

reason.description: Why it asks, as the agent wrote it. Text only, from an agent: a client draws it as plain text, never as markup, and drops control characters. Optional.

note.description: The founder's note on the decision (why it was rejected, say), as hr.decide took it. Absent when the founder gave none or it is still open.

asked.description: The fields the proposal asks for (vendor, model, effort, team, repo, to, then each `set <key>`). Every value is text from an agent (same rule as `reason`); optional, and a key it did not ask for is absent. Absent for kind bundle: its `diff` carries the changes. members, repos, relation, response and context texts are in `diff` only.

to.description: rename: the new name; link, unlink: the other end.

sets.description: `set <key>`: each agent setting asked for, key to value.

oneOf.description: Why the change did not go through; set when state is apply_failed and an apply ran and failed, else null. Text only; the daemon cuts it at 400 characters. Optional.
When it was decided, withdrawn or its apply failed; null while open. Optional.

kind.description: What the proposal does: add, retire, rename, link, unlink, team, settings, context or bundle (several changes decided once). An open set: a client draws a word it does not know as text. Optional until the Python hr.list sends it; a client then reads the first word of `title`.

HrArgs.description: What the proposal changes, by kind (hl hr). Every kind needs name.

name.description: The agent the proposal is about (the new agent's name for add; a team's manager for team).

to.description: rename: the new name; link, unlink: the other end.

members.description: team: each a suffix (`sea` is `name.sea`) or a full name.

sets.description: settings: agent setting keys as AgentSettingValues names them. context: whole new file texts keyed `ROLE.md` or `base.md`; empty text or control characters other than tab and newline is bad_request.

items.description: A step: kind (add, retire, rename, link, unlink, team, context) and the other fields of this type, name included.

changes.description: bundle: the steps, at most 40, each judged against the roster the earlier ones leave. name is then ignored (send the count, `3 changes`).

error.description: Why the agent's `schedules` value cannot be read, as `hl schedule list` says it.

methods.name: team.seal
methods.summary: The founder seals team.yaml and every agent.yaml as they are now (the Team page of the app); dry_run names what would be sealed.
methods.description: Seals are what lets the daemon tell a file the founder approved from one changed behind their back. The call without `dry_run` is the go-ahead and seals every file that is not sealed as it is, and marks the seals as begun; a file already matching its seal is left. A dry run lists each file it would take on, `new` (no seal before) or `changed` (it did not match its seal), with the digest it would be sealed with, and writes nothing and records nothing. Nothing to seal is `ok` true with that said. An agent's session is refused by role.

ok.description: Always true: a refusal is an error.

plan.description: Dry run only: one line per file that would be sealed (its label, why, its digest), or that nothing needs sealing.

said.description: Without dry_run: one line per file sealed, or that nothing needed sealing.

methods.name: hr.propose
methods.summary: Propose a roster change; the founder decides (hl hr add, retire, rename, link, unlink, team, settings, context, and diff, which is kind bundle: args.changes lists several changes decided once and applied together or not at all).

methods.name: hr.withdraw
methods.summary: Take back an undecided proposal: its author's own, or any for the founder; another agent is refused (gate role).

methods.name: trust.propose
methods.summary: Propose declaring a folder ocp may answer Claude's trust prompt in (hl trust add); the founder's own call declares it.
methods.description: Called by an agent it raises a decision for the founder, `why` required, and answers the proposal's id; called by the founder it declares the root directly, `why` optional (default `added by the founder`), and answers no proposal. A root already inside a declared one, a missing why or a decision that could not be raised is refused with the store's words. A paired device is refused, gate role. `root` must be an absolute path (bad_request, field `root`): the daemon would read a relative one, or `~`, against its own folder and home, so the client resolves it against its own.

methods.name: trust.list
methods.summary: Declared trust roots, and with proposals the proposals (hl trust list, hl trust proposals).

request.description: The decision request that asked the founder.

proposals.description: Empty unless `proposals` is true. State is the store's word (proposed, applied, rejected...).

declared.description: The same roots as `roots`, in the same order, with why and who added each.

methods.name: trust.remove
methods.summary: Drop a declared root (hl trust remove); needs no approval.
methods.description: The founder's: the declared roots live in the protected store, which an agent session cannot write, so an agent calling `hl trust remove` is refused today and by this method (gate role). A root that is not declared is not_found. `root` must be an absolute path, as for trust.propose (bad_request, field `root`).

methods.name: team.get
methods.summary: Agents, roles, allowed edges, role and base file metadata.

methods.name: hr.list
methods.summary: HR proposals with their diff: what waits for the founder, and what settled recently.

schema.description: Only the proposals in that state; without it, the list below.

methods.description: Without `state`: every proposal that waits (open, applying, and apply_failed until it is decided again) and every settled one (approved, rejected, withdrawn) from the last 7 days, at most 50 of those. Order: the waiting ones first, oldest `created` first; then the settled ones, newest `settled` first. A client counts the dot from `open` and `apply_failed`, never from `applying`. With `state`, only that state, in the same order, and no 7-day or 50 bound. A proposal whose requested_by is human (the founder's own change) is listed as any other, so a held one shows while it waits. The Python store's states map as: proposed = open; approved = apply_failed (it holds the founder's approval and the change is not applied: `error` is set when an apply ran and failed, null when it never ran, e.g. a crash between the two); applied = approved; rejected = rejected; withdrawn = withdrawn; enacting and failed are never listed.

methods.name: hr.decide
methods.summary: Approve or reject a proposal; approving an apply_failed one applies it again. Approving a change to an agent with a session running is accepted, not refused: the proposal turns applying, `said` names the agents whose turn it waits on, and the change is applied when those turns end. Refused with gate proposal_changed or proposal_settled, carrying the proposal as it is; an applying proposal is refused proposal_settled.

params.name: subject
params.description: Required for approve: the proposal's `subject` from hr.list. Refused if the proposal changed since.

methods.name: hr.apply_now
methods.summary: Apply a waiting HR change now: for an applying proposal, interrupt the turn of each agent in `waiting_on` (as session.interrupt does), then close the session, apply the change and restart the renamed agent at the next tick, without waiting for the turn to end. Returns at once with `said` naming the agents; the proposal stays applying until the change is applied (watch the hr topic). Refused with gate proposal_settled, carrying the proposal as it is, unless the proposal is applying. Works for every kind a running session can hold: rename, retire, context, link, settings.

methods.name: schedules.list

errors.description: Present only when an agent's `schedules` value cannot be read: that agent, and why.

methods.description: An agent whose `schedules` value is bad is listed in `errors` (target and the error text), not shown as an agent with no schedules.
